findings.evidence: Wave-B capture summary network_change_status reports 2 POSTs /api/admin/kds-order/change-status/{69,70} with status=202 and duration=3094ms / 3116ms. Both crossed the 2000ms threshold and SHOULD have been logged to per-state network.json per protocol §artifact-quartet. Actual: every per-state network.json is empty (state 02..08) or contains only the 422 (state 01). The spec instrumented network events into the capture.json summary only, not into the artifact files an adversarial reviewer reads. Without summary cross-reference an adversarial reviewer would (a) miss the 3s duration, (b) miss the POST counts, (c) under-verify S-2 single-PATCH claim.

findings.evidence: POST /api/admin/kds-order/change-status/69 took 3094ms (capture.json observations line: 'state05 order#69 POST result: status=202 elapsed=3094ms'). Per protocol §7 request duration > 2000ms requires .spinner / .skeleton / [aria-busy=true] during that window. The kds-card__cta button shows no spinner; it just becomes disabled or the toast appears immediately. Screenshot 05 shows the toast already visible during the 3s window, which serves as implicit loading feedback — but the CTA button itself stays in its normal state, so the chef cannot tell if their click is being processed (could double-tap). The 3s POST delay is itself suspect — backend response time is borderline.
findings.fix_hint: Two parts: (a) add aria-busy='true' on .kds-card__cta during pendingPostsByOrderId[orderId]==true (already tracked in store), and a 1px shrinking progress bar inside the button; (b) investigate why /api/admin/kds-order/change-status takes 3s — check StateMachine + outbox.write_then_dispatch + appendAuditChain time. notes: Wave B Round 1 KDS adversarial review of 8 states. Cross-validation of explicit prompted checks: (1) S-1 auto-PREPARING — PASS, both orders arrive on KDS with status pill 'En cours' = backend status 7 (PREPARING), confirmed in capture.json (server_statuses pre-bump: 69|status=7, 70|status=7); (2) S-2 1-clic CTA + single POST — PASS, capture.json records exactly 1 POST per order with status 202; (3) R-1 no 429 throttle — PASS, zero 429 in any network.json or console.json; (4) Q-4 no allergen banner — PASS, zero rendered allergen badges (only kds-card__allergen-spacer placeholders); (5) order contents match fixture — PASS, Order#69='Sandwich Cayenne/Tacos/Coca-Cola 33cl' and Order#70='Sandwich Cayenne/Big Cayenne/Petite Frites' verified by DOM extraction; (6) French Annuler aria-label — PASS, button has aria-label='Annuler la dernière commande marquée prête'; (7) kds-card--ready class applied with opacity:0.7 — PASS structurally but P2/P3 contrast/signal issues raised. NF525 chain bit-identical (pre=post hash 2a9270aa...). 0 P0 = no production blocker. 5 P1 must close before convergence: B-001 toast overlap, B-002 elapsed truncation, B-003 i18n leak, B-006 console pollution, B-007 misleading central banner. Verdict AMBER — caisse-to-KDS flow is operationally green but the visual/UX hygiene around the toast and the persistent banner is the dominant friction a chef will hit in production. Suggest a single heal sprint clustering B-001/B-002/B-007 (header + toast geometry) as one fix and B-003/B-006 (i18n) as a second.
